observations.text: SP performed the en-route descent to the standard required for this block, initiating the descent and reducing power only after the IP had identified the descent point and directed the profile. Once established, altitude was contained within 250 feet and airspeed within 15 KIAS, and the level-off required no additional prompting. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent identification of the descent point after receipt of the ATC clearance is expected to develop on the following sorties.

SP, having obtained the ATC clearance, commenced the en-route descent and tracked the assigned radial with the descent point and the level-off lead point supplied by the IP's verbal prompts only. Deviations reached the 300 feet and 20 KIAS limits and were recognized and corrected with delay, but without any IP intervention on the controls. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP initiated the en-route descent at the cleared point without prompting and used the radio navigation presentation to remain on the assigned course. Minor deviations of 200 feet in altitude and 15 KIAS in airspeed were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the en-route descent after the ATC clearance with accurate power management and a steady rate of descent. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 7 KIAS and the assigned radial within 3 degrees throughout the descent and the level-off. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the en-route descent in an impeccable manner, anticipating the level-off lead point and adjusting power without any delay. Deviations were negligible, with altitude within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 KIAS and course within 1 degree of the cleared radial. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect power and pitch technique at descent initiation, did not establish the planned rate of descent or maintain the assigned airspeed during the en-route descent, with the result that airspeed diverged by 25 KIAS and the level-off altitude was passed by 400 feet. The IP directed the power setting and executed part of the level-off.

SP, due to workload management that left the NAVAID tuning and identification unfinished before the descent, did not track the assigned radial while descending under the ATC clearance, with the result that the aircraft diverged 16 degrees from the cleared course. The IP had to direct the correction and take the controls to regain the airway centerline. The divergence was not recognized by the SP before the IP's intervention.

SP completed the en-route descent to the standard required for this block, with the descent point and the level-off lead point identified only after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and airspeed deviation 20 KIAS, both corrected with delay after those prompts and without IP intervention on the controls. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of altitude and airspeed trends without prompting is expected on the following sorties.

SP, after obtaining the ATC clearance, initiated the en-route descent at the planned point and maintained the assigned radial with the radio navigation aids without prompting. Minor deviations of 190 feet in altitude and 14 KIAS in airspeed during the descent were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP computed the descent point from the navigation aid and executed the en-route descent with accurate power reduction and a constant rate of descent. Altitude was contained within 90 feet, airspeed within 6 KIAS and the assigned course within 3 degrees, and the level-off was completed without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the en-route descent with exceptional accuracy, cross-checking altitude, airspeed and course continuously against the radio navigation presentation. Deviations were negligible, at 40 feet in altitude, 3 KIAS in airspeed and 1 degree of course, and the level-off was anticipated precisely. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a late lead point and a rate of descent that was not reduced approaching the assigned altitude, did not begin the transition to level flight in time, with the result that the level-off altitude was passed by 450 feet before any correction began. The IP directed the recovery and set the power for the level-off.

SP, due to absorption in the NAVAID retuning that left the descent rate unmonitored, did not maintain the assigned airspeed or the cleared radial during the en-route descent, with the result that airspeed deviated by 28 KIAS and the aircraft was 14 degrees off course. The IP took the controls to re-establish the descent profile. The deviations were not identified by the SP without assistance.

SP, due to an imprecise power setting after the descent was initiated, did not stabilize the airspeed in the descent, with the result that airspeed reached the 20 KIAS limit and altitude at level-off deviated by 300 feet. Both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the navigation display, did not monitor heading against the assigned radial during the en-route descent, with the result that the course deviated by 10 degrees and altitude by 300 feet. The correction was applied only after the IP's verbal prompt and the deviation was recognized with delay. No IP intervention on the controls was required.

SP executed the en-route descent within the desired standards, establishing the descent after the ATC clearance and tracking the assigned radial with the radio navigation aids. Deviations of 200 feet in altitude and 15 KIAS in airspeed occurred twice during the descent and were each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter airspeed control through the power reduction is expected to improve with practice.

SP computed the descent point correctly and executed the en-route descent with accurate power management and a constant rate of descent. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 KIAS and the assigned course within 4 degrees, and the level-off was completed without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the en-route descent with exceptional precision, anticipating both the descent point and the level-off lead point from the radio navigation presentation. Deviations were negligible, at 50 feet in altitude, 2 KIAS in airspeed and 1 degree of course. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect application of the descent checks and an omitted power reduction, did not establish the en-route descent profile required by the ATC clearance, with the result that airspeed deviated by 30 KIAS and the level-off altitude was passed by 500 feet. The IP directed the sequence and executed part of the level-off.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the cleared route, did not identify the correct radio navigation aid before commencing the en-route descent, with the result that the descent was flown 18 degrees off the cleared radial. The IP directed the retuning and identification and took the controls to regain the assigned course. The error was not detected by the SP without assistance.

SP, due to a rate of descent that was not adjusted for the remaining altitude, did not begin the level-off at the computed lead point, with the result that altitude deviated by 300 feet and airspeed by 20 KIAS at the transition to level flight. Both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established in the descent, did not maintain the instrument cross-check on altitude and course, with the result that the aircraft deviated 10 degrees from the assigned radial and 300 feet from the cleared altitude. Recognition came only after the IP's verbal prompt and the correction was applied with delay. The descent was completed without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to a coarse power reduction at descent initiation, did not stabilize the airspeed at the planned value during the en-route descent, with the result that airspeed deviated by 16 KIAS and altitude by 200 feet at the level-off. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not maintain the assigned radial with the required accuracy while descending, with the result that the course deviated by 8 degrees and altitude by 220 feet. The deviations were identified on the SP's own cross-check and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP executed the en-route descent accurately and promptly after the ATC clearance, using the radio navigation aids to remain on the assigned course. Altitude was held within 140 feet and airspeed within 9 KIAS, close to the limits of the desired standard, and the level-off required no prompting. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter altitude and airspeed cross-check through the descent is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP executed the en-route descent in an impeccable and standardized manner, planning the descent point and the level-off lead point from the radio navigation presentation and managing power without any delay. Deviations were negligible, at 40 feet in altitude, 2 KIAS in airspeed and 1 degree of course, demonstrating accuracy above the desired standard. Above end of block MIF achieved.
